quest.title: Sounds From Afar
quest.description: As the harvest season arrives, the Mondstadt's Adventurers' Guild has received a great number of requests from the citizenry. You and Paimon have also arrived back in the city in response to Katheryne's call for aid...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Festive Fever x50, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: Of Ballads and Brews: Act I
chapter.title: Sounds From Afar

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Let me just confirm... Yes, all tasks on the checklist are complete. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, we are grateful for your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Thank goodness you were able to come as soon as we contacted you. Who knows how we would have coped with all these commissions otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, it was nothin'! The last couple of days have been pretty busy, but it was all super easy stuff like delivering and escorting goods.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When we heard that you were short on people, we thought we were gonna be in for another long and drawn-out adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Being the seasoned adventurers that you are, it's true that you are suited to work of a much higher caliber than your recent assignments. However, this situation is unavoidable in Mondstadt at this time of year.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Probably because it's harvest season?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, that's right. This is the ideal season for harvesting crops and fruits, and for the wine capital of Teyvat, it's also the all-important wine-making season.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Farmers are anxious to sell off their fresh produce, and all the major wine merchants are seeking to purchase top-quality ingredients to make new product.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh. Well, no wonder we keep hearing people talking about wine these days.

dialogues.speaker: Fynn
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? Seriously?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Yes, I swear, I'm not making this up. The Acting Grand Master wants everyone to gather at headquarters, in the main hall. Hurry! We need to leave right now, or we'll be late!

dialogues.speaker: Fynn
dialogues.text: Hey, wait up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why do those two Knights look so... flustered?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: #Well hello there, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon. What a rare pleasure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaeya, just the person we need! Um, why is everyone running off to the Knights of Favonius headquarters all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And is our help required, too?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha, don't worry, this isn't one of those occasions where you need to come to everyone's rescue.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: All that's happened is that the Knights of Favonius have just received a letter from the Grand Master. Acting Grand Master Jean will be convening a meeting in the main hall shortly to go through it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, well that's a relief. ...Wait, hold on a second. What did you say, again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius? That's... Isn't that Varka? The leader of that legendary expedition!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what did Varka say in the letter? How's the expedition going? When are they getting back?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Oho, so interested in our Grand Master all of a sudden? Never knew you were such a gossip.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's only normal, isn't it? Bet you'd be curious too if there was someone you'd heard loads about but never met! Even Master Jean says he's a living legend... Pretty hard not to get hyped up after hearing that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, the expedition has been going on for aaaages, and we've still never heard a single thing about what they're up to.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hahaha, the Acting Grand Master is very gracious in her appraisal.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Varka brought quite a bit of trouble to those around him on the road to becoming a legend. I'll have to tell you about it sometime.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Anyway, since this has piqued your interest, why don't you join me at headquarters, and we'll see what the letter says?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: We do miss our Honorary Knight, after all. It's been quite a long time since your last visit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, let's go and see what it's all about. Bye, Katheryne, see ya soon.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Alright, take care now.

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hmm, it looks like just about everyone's here.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hey there, cutie, Paimon, I didn't know you two would be coming. So you heard about the letter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, we ran into Kaeya near the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon's never seen so many people in the main hall at once before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's getting kinda nervous now...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha, don't get too carried away, alright? If I know the Grand Master, the fact that he has the time to be writing letters means it's probably nothing serious. It certainly won't be bad news.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Kaeya's exaggerating a little, but otherwise I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: After all, Mika's not the kind of person who'd be able to keep it hidden if something were the matter. The truth would be written all over his face.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mika? Who's that?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Over there, look. The kid standing next to Jean in front of the staircase.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: He used to be a land surveyor in Eula's team. He's very talented in what he does and a very reliable person. When the expedition team set out, the Grand Master appointed him to be the core member of the front-line team.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: He's the one that brought back the letter.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Please may I have your attention, everyone. Now that we're all here, let's begin reading out the letter from the Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Mika, please go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Y—Yes, Master Jean!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Right... *clears throat* Hello, everybody, I am Mika, surveyor of the Reconnaissance Company. Uh, recently, I have been taking part in an assignment with the expedition team. I will now be reading Grand Master Varka's letter aloud for you all.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Ahem. "To the Knights of Favonius: Greetings, everyone. This is Varka."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "The first thing I want to say to you all is: Please put your minds at ease, the expedition is safe and all of its members are accounted for."

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: That's fantastic news!

dialogues.speaker: Fynn
dialogues.text: Phew, my palms are sweating...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Umm... May I continue?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Go ahead, Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "Alright, now that your fears are allayed, I trust you'll be ready to listen to the rest of my letter. I'm writing to you from the northernmost reaches of Teyvat by the light of a stove. The expedition forces are stationed here while we restock."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "I once told you that the purpose of this expedition was related to a dangerous secret from days long past. I am still unable to disclose more than this, but suffice to say that you needn't worry about how our mission is progressing."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "In the past couple of months, we received an unexpected visitor: the Fatui Harbinger known as 'The Captain.'"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? "The Captain"?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "I am fully aware of the Fatui's outrageous actions in Mondstadt in recent history. Nevertheless, The Captain was not hostile towards us on this occasion."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "Open parenthesis: I rather suspect that's because this time, Snezhnaya and we are in the same boat. Close parenthesis."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "The man hides everything under the mask he wears, so no one can know his past or his origins. However, one thing is for sure: He is as hard as iron for having the courage to challenge gods as an ordinary mortal."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "I don't doubt that he could even take out a Ruin Guard by stabbing it in its big, glowing eye with one of Klee's crayons. Open parenthesis: Don't get any ideas. Close parenthesis."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "Our scouts have confirmed that The Captain received orders to head for Natlan three days ago. We'll be able to sleep much better now that we don't need to worry about him anymore."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "I will admit that some of his actions have helped us. But even then, he owed us at least that much."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "This year's Weinlesefest must be kicking off in Mondstadt any day now? What a great pity that this year, once again, we will be unable to spend the festival together."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "Everyone here is always thinking back fondly upon the fine wines of Mondstadt, as well as all the happy times we have spent with each and every one of you."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "I hope that you and all the citizens of Mondstadt enjoy the festival to the fullest. Have a few drinks on our behalf — the Dawn Winery's limited-edition Weinlesefest seasonal special will do nicely."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "May Lord Barbatos bless Mondstadt, and may the wind carry our sentiments back to your side. Varka."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "P.S.: If you're wondering who's tougher between me and The Captain, well, I'm the Grand Master! There are ten captains in the Knights of Favonius but only one Grand Master, ahahahaha." His laugh, not mine.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: The letter ends here. Thank you, everyone, for your attention.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Master Jean, um... I just noticed that there's something else written on the back of the last page...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: "P.P.S.: I ran out of paper, so I'll add this here. Lisa, the following is a message for you." ...Oh, this part seems to be from the Grand Master to Miss Lisa.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Oh? For me?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ah, seeing that it's a special message... Lisa, we'll discuss this in private.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Everyone, as the Grand Master mentioned in his letter, the Weinlesefest is in just a few days. And how fortunate we are at this time to receive word that all is well with the expedition.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Though they are unable to return to Mondstadt and spend the festival with us, the Weinlesefest will nonetheless be a major event that all of Mondstadt is looking forward to.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I hope that everyone will guard your stations and perform your duties, both for our far-flung colleagues involved in the expedition, and also for the hardworking people of Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: And of course, during your time off, I hope you will be able to rest, relax, and enjoy this long-awaited festival.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: That brings our meeting to a close. Dismissed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Paimon hear that right? They ran into the Fatui's "Captain"...? Hmm... who knows what that was about, but it must have been important...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But ehh, Fatui Schmatooey, the real big deal here is the Weinlesefest — sounds like there'll be loads of free food and drink! Paimon wants to hear more!

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hey, cuties. How about we go and chat with Jean? You didn't get a chance to say a proper hello with so many people here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good! Alright, let's go.

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Master's office

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ah, Lisa. The Grand Master's letter is just on the table.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's been a long time. Apologies, I didn't get the chance to talk with you during the meeting just now.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: If you don't have any plans in the immediate future, why not stay in Mondstadt for a while? We'll be celebrating the Weinlesefest very soon.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Don't be deceived — Jean may appear very composed, but she's been missing you both terribly recently.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: *sigh* Lisa...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hehe... I'll leave you to catch up. I'm going to read my letter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Mondstadt's where our journey began, after all. We have a lot of fond memories here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Master Jean — neither of us really knows anything about this Weinlesefest... Could you tell us more about it?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Yes, of course.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The Weinlesefest is an ancient Mondstadt festival, just like Ludi Harpastum and Windblume. In addition, it's the most important part of the fall.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Each fall, the west wind blows in Mondstadt. Legend has it that the wonderful scent of Mondstadt's wine-making during the harvest season entices even the Anemo Archon into attendance, being the great wine-lover that he is.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: No matter where he is, he will transform into a soft breeze and return to his homeland.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Yeah, that sounds like the Anemo Archon, alright...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: For this reason, Mondstadters call the western wind the "returning wind." The Weinlesefest originally began as a celebration to welcome Lord Barbatos on his return.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: In the past, every household would brew fresh wine around this time of year, and keep it sealed at least until Windcoming Day during the following year's Weinlesefest.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Uncasking the sealed wine is a symbolic way of inviting the Anemo Archon to share a drink. Legend holds that if the Anemo Archon is satisfied with the taste of the wine, he will summon a gentle breeze to richly bless the people.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Richly bless"? How?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Knowing him, it was probably blessing them with more good wine the next year.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: That's a good question... But there's really no way of knowing.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: These are very old stories. Many of the details have been lost to time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, that'll happen! Some stories change completely as they get passed down... Hence why these days, Mondstadters will get into endless arguments over what kind of flower a Windblume is...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: All part of how cultural heritage is created.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Indeed. But for the time being, at least, the tradition of paying tribute to the Anemo Archon on Windcoming Day is still alive and well, and the Weinlesefest remains a time for Mondstadters to share the joy of the harvest with one another as they partake of fine wines.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: This is a time of the year when many Mondstadters living away from Mondstadt return to their hometown. For those unable to return, Weinlesefest is the period when they miss their family and friends most keenly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So that's why the Grand Master wrote: "May the wind carry our sentiments back to your side."

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: For this year, we've joined forces with the Church of Favonius and the Adventurers' Guild to host a celebration on the banks of Cider Lake, just outside of Springvale. There will also be a traditional Wine Market during the festival period.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Wine Market"?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Well, originally it was simply a place where winemakers and farmers would come to trade in raw ingredients for wine-making.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: These days, it is a much grander affair. Not only will you find a range of choice wines, but seasonal fruit beverages and food items for everyone to enjoy, too. A lot of people also sell second-hand goods and handicrafts at the market.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The Knights of Favonius plan to use this as an opportunity to do some fundraising for needy children and elderly people in the city.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow. Sounds pretty cool.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: If you have the time, I encourage you to take a look around. I hope you'll find it a worthwhile experience. Now, Lisa — what was the Grand Master's message to you about?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I was just about to bring that up. The Grand Master says he wants me to handle something for him — something to do with Razor's past.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Razor's past?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor told us that he was raised by a pack of wolves in Wolvendom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He never knew his parents. In his own words, the wolf pack is his "lupical," which means family.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Yes, that was as much as I knew as well.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: But in his letter, the Grand Master says that in the cabinet above the third bookshelf to the right of the grandfather clock in Jean's office, there's a wooden box containing some items that Razor's parents left for him. He says... "It's time to give the box to Razor."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does this mean the Grand Master knew Razor's parents?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: It would seem so. The Grand Master didn't simply run into Razor one day in Wolvendom and teach him how to use a sword. No, the connection between them goes back much further.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Well c'mon, let's go find Razor! He'll be pretty excited to find out something about his true parents!

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Oh, cutie. Nothing escapes your eyes, does it?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: For the child who never met their biological parents, this kind of conversation is always a difficult one. Even for the most well-adjusted.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: By contrast, Razor grew up in Wolvendom and has had very limited contact with human society... Who knows whether he's ready for this or not.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I'm sure the Grand Master will have given due consideration to Razor's circumstances. Perhaps he felt that now would be the most appropriate time.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hmm, that's a good point. Okay, cuties, can I leave you to break the news to Razor?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: He thinks of me as his teacher, so he might not open up to me if he gets upset. But you are his trusted friends. I think it makes more sense for him to hear about this from you.

choices.text: Don't worry, leave this to us.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Thank you, sweetie.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Try to be as encouraging as you can. Someone his age needs all the love and support they can get.

choices.text: We'll talk it out with Razor.

talks.objective: Leave the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look, it's a hunting trap. It looks like the ones that the hunters from Springvale use...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are traces of Electro energy near the trap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Electro energy? Hmm, Paimon wonders if it could be Razor. But, Paimon thought he was pretty good at avoiding the hunters...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well anyway, let's follow the traces of Electro and see where they lead.

talks.objective: Use Elemental Sight to trace Electro

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Alright! The last trap has been set. Razor, thanks for coming with me all this way.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: It's okay. My legs are strong. ...Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: What is it, Razor?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: *sniff* It smells... familiar. Friend, from far away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Razor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and it's Draff, too! Are you two hunting together?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Yes, it's almost harvest season, and the boars are venturing into the towns and wineries looking for food.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: They're trampling crops and destroying the vineyards. Someone could get seriously hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius came to us asking for help keeping the boars a safe distance away from the population.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I and Uncle Brown Cat, catch boars, protect everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Razor, this is a big step for you! Paimon remembers you used to hide away from the hunters.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Hehe, you can say that again! Razor was the star of the show this time. He let the wolves know we'd be coming, so we were able to get through Wolvendom without anyone getting hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Helping everyone, helping lupical, makes me happy. But... much talking. Very tired now.

choices.text: Still, it's a sign of progress.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! But, um... Actually, we came here today because we have some really important news...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Razor about Varka's letter...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I... don't know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor... Do you mean, you don't want to know about your real parents?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I want to know, but... don't want to know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... So you do wanna know, but at the same time, you don't wanna know? Sounds complicated...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Traveler, come and take a look at the trap I just placed. Let's give Razor some space to process things.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Yes, I have some thoughts about all this after seeing how Razor reacted.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: We've been hunting together a lot recently. The kid might not talk much, but still, I feel like I've come to understand him a little over the time we've spent together.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Here's what I think... He definitely wants to find out about his parents. It's just that his fear of the unknown is overwhelming everything else he's feeling.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: I'm a father myself, so I know a thing or two about kids.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: You know, when Diona was little, if I got back late from a hunt one night, she'd be watching me like a hawk for days afterwards, as if she was worried that I might abandon her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you mean Razor's worried that he was abandoned by his own parents...?

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Exactly. I think that's the heart of it. And if it turns out they did, well, I don't think there's anything we could say to console him. That's not my only concern, though...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Razor is developing at his own pace. There are lots of issues that can't be solved all in one go, but he's making progress, one step at a time.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: But now this thing with his parents is added into the mix... It might push him to want to figure out once and for all where he comes from and where he's going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like a similar take to Lisa's. Maybe all mature adults think like this, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but then again... Master Jean had a different view. She said it's more about trusting other people and in your own instincts!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uhh... {NICKNAME}, what do you think?

choices.text: He'll have to face this sooner or later...

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Gotcha. Well, knowing that he's got a friend like you to rely on makes me feel much better about this whole thing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, how about this:

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Paimon about how you plan to approach the situation...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, got it! Right, let's head back. We don't wanna keep him waiting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Razor... So, what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Still thinking... My heart, it feels strange... like being stabbed by Wolfhook.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you think of Varka?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Varka? Hmm... Tall, very strong, likes to laugh.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then... do you trust Varka?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes. Trust.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...He's very good to me. Give me a name, teach me to fight. But now... busy with important work... I miss him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, Razor, Varka used up all the paper writing this letter, but he still made sure he found room on the back to add a note for Lisa. He specifically told her to give you the things that your parents left for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means that he thinks the items have a special meaning for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But more importantly than that... Whatever happens, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Lisa, and all your other friends will always be here for you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: That's right! And old Uncle Brown Cat's here to support you as well.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...Okay. Thank you. I decide... I want to go with you, to see teacher.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Haha, that's the spirit, kiddo!

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Well, you folks had better be heading off, then. I'm just about finished here, so I'll be heading home very shortly myself. I'd better try and get plenty of father-daughter time in before the Weinlesefest starts, hahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye, Draff, see you again next time.

choices.text: I will be there for him as a friend through this...
Seems like you have something to say.

talks.objective: Go back to the Grand Master's office

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lisa, we've brought Razor.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Hello, Teacher. I'm here, to see the box.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Ah, my little wolf cub's in a good mood. I'm assuming they've discussed the whole story with you already?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Here, this is it, the wooden box. I haven't touched it, except for taking it out of the cabinet. When you're sure you're ready, you can open it yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Yes, I am sure.

dialogues.speaker: The wooden box
dialogues.text: *click*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... This is just a pile of junk. Paimon thought there'd at least be a letter, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh, you don't think that... after all this time, Varka might be getting mixed up between different boxes?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: *sniff* There is a scent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A scent? What kind?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: A scent I remember from a long, long time ago. It's... their scent.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Human scent... Father and mother's scent.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Incredible... You still remember scents from all the way back in your childhood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you really have a good sense of smell, Razor. Guess being wild by nature has its advantages... Let's see what other leads we can find!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, this woolen hand puppet looks kinda wonky. Guess it must be handmade, huh... Is this a part from a Ruin Guard?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Hey, look, this wine bottle is still half full!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there's a note stuck on it: "Thousand," uh... "Thousand-Wind Wine."

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Oh? So it's a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Teacher, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Of course. Thousand-Wind Wine was the first kind of wine that Mondstadters ever learned to make, or so they say.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: As to how it got its name, some say it's a reference to the numerous ingredients used to make it, while others say it's because every bottle tastes slightly different.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I remember reading somewhere that there are all sorts of weird and wonderful ways of brewing it, and that it's very difficult to ensure it comes out tasting the same each time.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: This all makes it impractical to commercialize. Wine merchants are much more comfortable working with reliable, consistent-tasting products.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: That's why you'll almost never see Thousand-Wind Wine in the markets or taverns.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: In fact, it looks like your parents brewed this bottle themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must mean there's something pretty important about it... Ooh, Paimon has an idea! Razor, you've got a good nose. Why don't you open it up and take a whiff? Maybe it'll tell you something!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, he seems really in the zone... and is that a smile?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Sweet, cold, a little bitter... I like. Many things, all mixed together.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: But, things in wine, smell different...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even you can't tell what it is, Razor?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I will try again.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: It's okay, Razor, don't push yourself too hard. What do we do when we try something and it doesn't work?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Try... another way.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: That's right. You still remember what I taught you.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: It's almost the Weinlesefest. Everyone who knows anything worth knowing about wine will be gathering in Mondstadt. Surely someone will know a thing or two about Thousand-Wind Wine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, great idea!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Will Venti be coming...?)

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Make sure you don't miss the opening ceremony, cutie. Everyone will be there. Razor, you should go too — it'll be a good opportunity to ask around.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Okay. Ask many people... I will try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll be right there with you. We can be your go-betweens. You know, like you were with the wolves, for Draff!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay. Then, I will go back now. I need to tell lupical about human mother and human father.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! See you at the opening ceremony!

choices.text: We'll be there with you. Just like we promised.

talks.objective: Wait for the Weinlesefest (08:00 – 10:00 two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone, for your patience. I am pleased to announce that this year's Weinlesefest has officially begun.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: We hope the residents of Mondstadt and visitors from all over will enjoy the magnificent wines and experience the joy of the harvest.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: When Windcoming Day arrives, we will hold a grand toasting ceremony to welcome the Anemo Archon, Barbatos, back home.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Let the Wind lead!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Let the Wind lead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Razor! You're here already.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Mmm... So many... people...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, let's sneak outta here. There's someone we gotta find!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Find? Who?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just some tone-deaf bard. But he's also a know-it-all and loves nothing more than drinking, so he might actually be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Tone-Deaf Bard!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, how do you do? Haha, I had a feeling I'd run into you soon, during this most enchanting of festivals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Spoken like a true poet... Hmm, but reading between the lines here — if one bottle is tipsy, and two is merry, just how many is "enchanting," exactly?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha, oh, don't say that. This festival has so much more to offer than just drinking.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Anyway, hey, Razor! How have you been?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Alright. I have... a question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Razor has something he wants to ask you about. Know anything about Thousand-Wind Wine?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ooh, now there's a name that takes me back. Let me think... how long has it been since I last heard someone mention Thousand-Wind Wine?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor's parents left him a box with a half-bottle of wine inside, and there's a label on it that says "Thousand-Wind Wine."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard there's a lotta history behind this type of wine, and the brewing methods go way, way back, so we figured you'd be a good person to ask.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: It smells good, but... don't know, what's inside.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I see, I see, so you want to know how Thousand-Wind Wine is made? Well, you came to the right person. I happen to know a little rhyme called... well, as it happens, "Thousand-Wind Wine."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I was going to save it for Windcoming Day, but far be it from me to deny an early serenade to a friend in need. How about it? Shall I recite it for you?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: A song... Not easy to understand, but still want to hear.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Excellent answer. Then, ahem, hear it you shall:

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"Fill up the barrels and store them away,
Then wait, wait for a windier day.
Wax the bottles, seal them tight,
For the south wind that soothes, for the north wind that bites."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"How does this fine wine taste to the tongue?
As 'Mondstadt' to the ear: like a sweet dream of freedom.
And what are the fruits that went into the brew?
An explorer's courage, a love tender and true."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"A defender's will, strong as yesteryear,
Joining the thousand winds in a song of good cheer,
Turning sour into sweet, bitter notes fade away,
As we wait, wait for a windier day."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehehe, thank you so much for the applause. Was the rhyme of help to you?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Like wine. A little sweet, but now, head spinning. Don't understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, it's not just you! That was supposed to be about wine-making, but it didn't give a single detail about the process!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, well, maybe it's a little abstract and romanticized, but that's one of the defining features of Mondstadt poetry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so let's try to pin this down. What did the poem say the ingredients are? Hmmm... Ummm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An explorer's courage, a love tender and true, a defender's will, and... the thousand winds'... "song of good cheer"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, Paimon has absolutely no idea what any of these refer to!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look, Tone-Deaf Bard, you clearly know what the whole thing means, so could you do us a favor and at least give us a hint?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You misunderstand me. I'm not trying to make you work for it or anything, but the lyrics are what they are. If there's anything they left out, even I can't fill in the blanks.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: If you want to know the secret behind this sweet scent, you might have to start by rolling up your sleeves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rolling up our sleeves...? You mean, we need to go and make this wine for ourselves, and somehow that'll teach us everything we wanna know? ...This better not be a prank!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: We've known each other for so long, and you still don't trust my intentions? Oh, the pain...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...I trust. I... want to try.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I want to... make wine, and find answers.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: If I know how to make wine, then I know what is in father and mother's wine.

choices.text: By reliving their actions, maybe we will understand...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Right.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I want to... know about them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you say so, Razor. Guess we'll have to take Tone-Deaf Bard's word on this one. We'll give it a try, and as first-time wine-makers, there's no shame if it turns out bad!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Don't worry, really. Freedom is the key here. It's not as hard as you might think.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As long as you add ingredients to the mix in a spirit of joy and sincerity, I promise you will reap the rewards you wish for.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I will tell poem to teacher.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Then... I need to think alone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the spirit. So, how about we meet again in two days? Let's say same place, right here?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay. I will remember. See you, then.

choices.text: So nice to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: As his teacher, I have a duty to give him the best education and guidance that I can. I'll make sure I'm prepared by the time you get back.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Go on now, cuties. I'll leave Razor in your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Ah! Uh, h—hi there, umm... You must be looking for Captain Kaeya...? Please, don't mind me!

choices.text: Actually, I was looking for you.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Huh? Wait, but... wha—!? Oh geez, Captain Kaeya... Wh—What should I say?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Haha, oh, Mika... How have you not changed one bit after being out on the front line this long?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: You were just asking me about the Stormterror incident, weren't you? Well, allow me to introduce you to the legendary Honorary Knight.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! And also the legendary Paimon!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: H—Hi there, you guys are so strong, I'm... I'm in awe. Um... I have to go and report in with Captain Eula now, please excuse me!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Mika leaves the Knights of Favonius in a hurry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, he just left... Well, that's too bad. Paimon was gonna ask him all about the expedition.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: That is a pity, it really is. But don't take it the wrong way. The way he sees it, every pair of eyes in Mondstadt is focused squarely on you.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Give it some time and this'll all sort itself out. Next time you see him, I'm sure you'll get along just fine.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: In fact, let me share a little secret with you: Try talking to him about exploring the wild. You'll win his trust in no time.

choices.text: I just wanted to say hi.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Well, what do you think? Glad you tagged along this time?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: A little birdie told me that you'll be staying in Mondstadt for the Weinlesefest? Hope you enjoy yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Can you believe the expedition party ran into The Captain of the Fatui? Whew... what a relief that nothing came of it.

dialogues.speaker: Fynn
dialogues.text: What's there to be afraid of? The Grand Master is there. One Grand Master should be able to take on at least, like... 10 Captains.

dialogues.speaker: Fynn
dialogues.text: Wait, forget that — you shouldn't be worrying about the expedition when you've got the Knights of Favonius charity fundraising booth that you're supposed to be organizing. So? How's it coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: *sigh* Actually... I still haven't really decided what to sell...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Oh, hi, Traveler. Back in Mondstadt for the Weinlesefest, huh? Well, watch out for boars if you're out exploring the open country.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Allan, Draff's apprentice! Um, have you seen Razor? You know — the young guy who lives in Wolvendom?

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Razor? Wait, who's that again... Oh! You mean the guy who goes hunting with Draff? I haven't actually seen him today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Well, there aren't any traces of Electro around here anyway. Let's try somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: As Razor's teacher, I'm so happy to see him taking this first step.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: And you must be tired from running around trying to find Razor. Why don't you rest here a while? I'll make you a nice cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, good. I was hoping we might get to chat some more.

choices.text: Can I hear the poem again?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You need a refresher? Okay, I'll perform the first half again.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"Fill up the barrels and store them away,
Then wait, wait for a windier day.
Wax the bottles, seal them tight,
For the south wind that soothes, for the north wind that bites."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"How does this fine wine taste to the tongue?
As 'Mondstadt' to the ear: like a sweet dream of freedom.
And what are the fruits that went into the brew?
An explorer's courage, a love tender and true."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"A defender's will, strong as yesteryear,
Joining the thousand winds in a song of good cheer,
Turning sour into sweet, bitter notes fade away,
As we wait, wait for a windier day."

choices.text: What are your thoughts on the Weinlesefest?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I am fond of each and every one of Mondstadt's festivals, but if I'm honest, Weinlesefest has an extra-special place in my heart.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You know, the Anemo Archon goes into a slumber after the west wind dies down, leaving the north wind to blow during the winter.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Which means, this festival is the big feast before the winter slumber!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I wouldn't worry yourself too much about him.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Staying true to their journey and discovering joy and freedom for themselves is what Mondstadters do best.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The same goes for you. You have to find the thing that makes you happy. Haha, mostly because your happiness is very important to me.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: See you around. Remember, there's no rush. Take your time, and you'll find all the answers that you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Razor's usually around Wolvendom, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, how do you think he'll react after hearing about this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there's another trap up ahead! And can you feel that Electro energy, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Electro traces lead deep into Wolvendom. Let's keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Raaazooor...! Are you there?
